oncall-bot: Pager triggered: embeddings-queue-high (P2) in ap-southeast-1 · elevated queue depth + backpressure · alerted at 1992504321. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-embeddings-asia :rotating_light:

Alex Chen: I'm taking primary for the next 30m, then handing to Morgan at 20:30 UTC. Quick summary: queue depth ~400 (normal  <50), sustained processing lag ~120s, autoscaler didn't add nodes because spot pool had recurring failures.

Priya Singh: Noted customer impact: a handful of enterprise tenants in APAC reporting timeouts for batch embeddings. We have 3 support tickets open (T-3412, T-3415, T-3420). High-level SLA risk for those tenants.

Eli Martinez: Mitigations in progress: 1) manual scale up to dedicated pool (nv4x64) underway, 2) enabled fallback to emb-small model for non-real-time jobs, 3) temporarily increased per-tenant rate limit to reduce pileup.

Alex Chen: Commands I ran:
```
# create extra worker nodes in dedicated pool
redwood infra scale --pool embeddings-apac-dedicated --count +4
# enable fallback route
redwood api route update --name embeddings --fallback emb-small-v2
```
Logs show node creation started but 2/4 nodes failed initial kubelet health check (caused by a corrupted AMI in that spot fleet).

Priya Singh: Runbook refs: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-backpressure (section 4 manual scale) and https://redwood.internal/runbooks/spot-pool-fallback. If autoscaler fails, use dedicated pool and set fallback to emb-small.

Morgan Patel: I'm on secondary. I can take over primary at 20:30 UTC. Coverage gap: Eli is offline 21:00-22:00 UTC; Priya will be reachable but on-call steps need an engineer to approve capacity bump. If Morgan and I overlap, we can handoff safely.

oncall-bot: Update: dedicated pool scale up step completed (4/4 nodes), but 2 nodes in the new pool flapped and were put into NotReady. Current healthy nodes +2 net.

Eli Martinez: Flapping nodes due to kernel incompatible with our inferred AMI kernel param. Ops infra is rolling a patched image to the pool; ETA ~18m. Meanwhile I pushed a temporary topology change: route a subset (10%) of traffic to eu-west-1 as failover for interactive jobs. Non-interactive batch still queued.

Alex Chen: Impact note for handoff: interactive endpoints ~95% healthy due to eu-west failover, batch embeddings backlog persists (expected drain ~2h at current processing). Customers affected: tenant-a (high), tenant-b (medium), tenant-c (low). Support notified.

Priya Singh: Open action items for next shift: 1) confirm patched AMI applied and flapping stops, 2) monitor queue depth -> target <100 before removing failover routing, 3) coordinate with platform to migrate stuck jobs to emb-small if SLA breach imminent, 4) update customers in T-3412/15/20 with ETA.

Morgan Patel: I'll take primary at 20:30 UTC. My contact: @morgan (mobile +1-555-0102). If dedicated pool fails to stabilize, escalate to platform@redwood (pager duty esc).

Alex Chen: Handoff: primary -> Morgan Patel (20:30 UTC). secondary -> Priya Singh. Bridge notes: use bridge link https://redwood.internal/bridges/brig-1992504321 for any live debugging. I've pinned the runbook section in the thread.

Eli Martinez: FYI: scheduled job that caused bulk resubmits was a cron from tenant-b that retried on 500s; support requested we temporarily throttle it. I added a temporary token-level throttle for tenant-b.

Priya Singh: Logging to watch: /var/log/embeddings/processor.log and redis queue length metric: embeddings.queue.depth.ap-southeast-1. Alert thresholds adjusted to warn at 200, page at 400.

Morgan Patel: Acknowledged. I'll confirm node health and queue drain after I take over. If anything changes before handoff I'll ping here. :thumbsup:

Alex Chen: Thanks team. Leaving this open for handoff; last update 1992507921.
